results.quote: with 31 binary columns for the presence of each sign type

results.claim: Germany contributes 264 records and France contributes 148 records to SignBase

results.quote: calculated the proportion of objects carrying each sign type in each country and counted the objects from each site

results.quote: analysed sample contains 108 objects (46 German, 62 French)

results.quote: most frequent sign type is notch in Germany and notch in France
results.claim: Notches are the most frequent sign type in both Germany and France

results.quote: German objects come from 9 sites and the French objects from 21

results.quote: Figure 1 shows how the common sign types are spread across these sites

results.quote: Castanet supplies 13% of the French ones
results.claim: Castanet supplies 13% of the French objects in the analyzed sample

results.quote: so a national difference may reflect the excavation and preservation history of a few sites

results.claim: Germany and France share common sign types and differ only in rare sign types

results.quote: Notches and lines are the two most frequent signs in both countries

results.quote: Notches appear on 57% of German objects and 45% of French objects

results.quote: lines on 35% and 35%

results.claim: Vulva signs appear only in France, on 8% of French objects

results.quote: so these few rare-sign contrasts do not yet show separate regional traditions
